st: The Whole Truth and Nothing But
d: A driven newspaper editor must choose between a shocking front page headline or her own sister's reputation.
After a man, who has been living in his father's shadow, inherits the family taffy factory to which he has never felt attached, he must choose whether or not to sell it.
When a woman's husband is murdered and she is left penniless, she must face returning to the bad neighborhood she worked so hard to flee.
On New Year's Eve, a melancholy woman races against time to fulfill a promise she made to her father 45 years earlier.
When an honest man makes a desperate mistake, he must face dire consequences that put his entire family in danger.
The Angels must help a troubled young boy who wants to divorce his parents.
The Angels attempt to save a troubled marriage when the neglected wife encounters a man with whom she was once in love.
At a time when the country is on the brink of peace, Monica brings a group of Northern Ireland teenagers, both Protestant and Catholic, to America to discover the true meaning of peace.
The Angels set out for a night of bowling and find enough needy patrons to "spare."
The Angels visit an art gallery where they help three people in need.
On the eve of a boy's bar mitzvah, he and his agnostic grandfather must come to terms with what it means to become a man.
The Angels help a female convict face the truth about a crime she does not believe she committed.
The Angels help a busy, all-American family when a crisis threatens to tear it apart.

st: Living The Rest Of My Life
d: The Angels help an older woman face the truth about her son and start living for herself.
Ricky is a gas station attendant who just lost his job. Monica goes to help with the closing inventory, and to convince him that a door closing opens another door and he needs to pursue his poetry.
Tess helps Monica see the repercussions of her angry behavior when it affects the lives of some innocent strangers.
The Angels help a young boy, living with his father in a traveling circus, come to terms with the fact that his father is a little person.
